t: The figures were buried with Qin Shi Huang in 210–209 BCE, laid out in military formation to guard his tomb from the east in the afterlife.
Heads, limbs and torsos were made separately, the faces from moulds, and clay was added after assembly to give each figure its own features, so that each face appears different.
Farmers digging a well found the first figures in 1974; most remain in situ, and the emperor’s tomb itself is still unopened, possibly over concerns for the preservation of its contents.
dyk: Once exposed to Xi’an’s dry air, the lacquer covering under the figures’ paint can curl in fifteen seconds and flake off in just four minutes.
ev: Work begins on the mausoleum of the future first emperor, then aged 13 and newly King of Qin
The terracotta army is buried with the emperor in his mausoleum
Farmers digging a well near Mount Li find the first figures, prompting archaeologists to investigate
The first exhibition of the figures outside China opens at the National Gallery of Victoria in Melbourne
Excavation of Pit K9901 uncovers the figures dubbed the Acrobats
A grave pit holding 121 skeletons attributed to the site’s workers is excavated
The British Museum opens “The First Emperor: China’s Terracotta Army”, which made 2008 its most successful year

f.made: Made for the mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang in workshops by government labourers and local craftsmen; Sima Qian says the mausoleum project involved 700,000 conscripted workers; the sculptors signed their names in the figures’ armpits, and each workshop inscribed its name on what it made
f.form: Life-sized terracotta figures, typically 1.75 to about 2 metres tall, of infantry, cavalry, charioteers, archers and officers, with chariots and horses, once painted and armed with real bronze weapons; estimated in 2007 at more than 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots with 520 horses and 150 cavalry horses in three pits
f.where: For the most part in situ, in pits about 1,500 m east of the emperor’s tomb mound at Mount Li in Lintong County, outside Xi’an, Shaanxi, under a museum complex; figures have travelled to exhibitions around the world
f.known: the largest pottery figurine group ever found; individual faces, no two figures exactly alike; ranks shown by height, uniform and hairstyle; more than 40,000 bronze weapons; the painted colours lost on exposure; the unopened tomb of the first emperor; the acrobats and other non-military figures
